register: Critical academic and media term for treating technical fixes as sufficient answers to complex political or social problems.
trap: Solutionnisme is not neutral problem-solving: it criticizes the reduction of political choices and structural conflicts to technical problems.
example_tl: Le solutionnisme technologique promet une application pour chaque crise sociale, mais élude les rapports de pouvoir et les responsabilités institutionnelles qui la structurent.
example_en: Technological solutionism promises an app for every social crisis, but evades the power relations and institutional responsibilities that structure it.
cloze: {{c1::Le solutionnisme technologique}} promet une application pour chaque crise sociale, mais élude les rapports de pouvoir et les responsabilités institutionnelles qui la structurent.
note: Old_back is accurate. The card fixes the term’s critical force and records the concise specialist alternative technosolutionnisme.

register: Specialist critical neologism, associated especially with analyses that treat an abstract internet as a single force with its own inherent logic.
trap: This is not political centrism practiced online; it names the habit of putting an abstract idea of the internet at the center of every explanation.
example_tl: L’internet-centrisme de certains réformateurs suppose que la connectivité démocratise mécaniquement la société, alors que les mêmes réseaux peuvent renforcer le contrôle autoritaire.
example_en: The internet-centrism of certain reformers assumes that connectivity automatically democratizes society, whereas the same networks can reinforce authoritarian control.
cloze: {{c1::L’internet-centrisme}} de certains réformateurs suppose que la connectivité démocratise mécaniquement la société, alors que les mêmes réseaux peuvent renforcer le contrôle autoritaire.
note: Materially repairs old_back: the French neologism is hyphenated and written as a single lexical unit, without internal capitalization or spacing. Self-review replaced an abstract possessor with the natural agentive réformateurs.

register: Established critical term in political economy and technology studies for a business logic based on extracting and monetizing behavioral data.
trap: It does not merely denote a market selling surveillance equipment; surveillance describes the system’s method of accumulating and predicting behavior.
example_tl: Le capitalisme de surveillance transforme chaque interaction en matière première comportementale, sans accorder aux usagers de contrôle effectif sur les usages ultérieurs de leurs données.
example_en: Surveillance capitalism turns every interaction into behavioral raw material without granting users effective control over the subsequent uses of their data.
cloze: {{c1::Le capitalisme de surveillance}} transforme chaque interaction en matière première comportementale, sans accorder aux usagers de contrôle effectif sur les usages ultérieurs de leurs données.
note: Old_back gives the established French term but unnecessarily capitalizes its article.

register: Neutral-formal term in research, algorithmic auditing and technology policy; the alternative is more explanatory and less terminological.
trap: Biais may arise from data, design or deployment context; préjugé algorithmique is too anthropomorphic and suggests an intentionally held opinion.
example_tl: Un biais algorithmique peut défavoriser systématiquement les candidates, même lorsque le modèle n’utilise pas le sexe comme variable explicite de décision.
example_en: Algorithmic bias can systematically disadvantage female candidates even when the model does not use sex as an explicit decision variable.
cloze: Un {{c1::biais algorithmique}} peut défavoriser systématiquement les candidates, même lorsque le modèle n’utilise pas le sexe comme variable explicite de décision.
note: Old_back is accurate; the example prevents the mistaken inference that only an explicitly protected variable can generate bias.

register: Established telecommunications-policy term in France; the Net form remains conventional in institutional and journalistic writing.
trap: The term does not claim that online content is politically neutral; it concerns nondiscriminatory treatment of traffic by network access providers.
example_tl: La neutralité du Net interdit à un fournisseur de ralentir un service rival ou de facturer aux plateformes un accès prioritaire à ses abonnés.
example_en: Net neutrality prohibits a provider from slowing a rival service or charging platforms for priority access to its subscribers.
cloze: {{c1::La neutralité du Net}} interdit à un fournisseur de ralentir un service rival ou de facturer aux plateformes un accès prioritaire à ses abonnés.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary initial capitalization; the example anchors the precise regulatory sense. Self-review clarified who charges whom for priority access.

register: Established data-protection and technology-policy term; the en construction is especially natural in France-French institutional prose.
trap: A courtier en données is not any neutral data intermediary: the label usually foregrounds collecting, combining and selling personal profiles.
example_tl: Les courtiers en données combinent des historiques d’achat, des données de localisation et des centres d’intérêt pour vendre des profils rarement consultables ou rectifiables par les personnes concernées.
example_en: Data brokers combine purchase histories, location data, and interests to sell profiles that the people concerned can rarely inspect or correct.
cloze: {{c1::Les courtiers en données}} combinent des historiques d’achat, des données de localisation et des centres d’intérêt pour vendre des profils rarement consultables ou rectifiables par les personnes concernées.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the established plural because the source denotes the industry’s actors, then made the types of brokered data and the access problem more precise.

register: Established media-criticism metaphor for informational isolation attributed specifically to personalized algorithmic selection.
trap: It is not identical to a chambre d’écho: the bubble emphasizes personalized filtering, while the chamber emphasizes mutual reinforcement within a group.
example_tl: Imputer toute la polarisation à la bulle de filtres occulte les conflits sociaux et les campagnes organisées qui nourrissent également les clivages politiques.
example_en: Attributing all polarization to the filter bubble obscures the social conflicts and organized campaigns that also fuel political divisions.
cloze: Imputer toute la polarisation à {{c1::la bulle de filtres}} occulte les conflits sociaux et les campagnes organisées qui nourrissent également les clivages politiques.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Materially improves old_back: the established term uses plural filtres. Self-review replaced divisions publiques with the idiomatic clivages politiques.

register: Established critical political-economy term; the singular is conventional as a classificatory label, while the plural foregrounds the platform sector.
trap: It denotes an economic formation organized around data, network effects and gatekeeping, not merely capitalism taking place inside one online platform.
example_tl: Le capitalisme de plateforme transfère les risques aux travailleurs et aux fournisseurs, tandis que les intermédiaires contrôlent les données, l’accès et les règles du marché.
example_en: Platform capitalism transfers risks to workers and suppliers while intermediaries control data, access, and market rules.
cloze: {{c1::Le capitalisme de plateforme}} transfère les risques aux travailleurs et aux fournisseurs, tandis que les intermédiaires contrôlent les données, l’accès et les règles du marché.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. The alternative records the common plural variant without displacing the conventional singular label.

register: Established but often promotional anglicism in innovation discourse; critical prose frequently questions whether the promised rupture is real.
trap: In this domain disruption is not a simple perturbation or service interruption; it claims a radical transformation of a market or institutional model.
example_tl: La disruption promise dans l’éducation a surtout privatisé des ressources publiques et rendu les établissements dépendants de plateformes propriétaires difficiles à quitter.
example_en: The disruption promised in education mainly privatized public resources and made institutions dependent on proprietary platforms that are difficult to leave.
cloze: {{c1::La disruption}} promise dans l’éducation a surtout privatisé des ressources publiques et rendu les établissements dépendants de plateformes propriétaires difficiles à quitter.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns the digital-economy sense to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Materially corrects old_back, whose perturbation misses the market-transformation claim.

register: Critical term in postcolonial studies and technology policy for asymmetric control of infrastructure, standards, data and extracted value.
trap: It is stronger than dépendance numérique: it frames infrastructural and data control as a structural relationship of domination and extraction.
example_tl: Le colonialisme numérique s’enracine lorsque des entreprises étrangères contrôlent les données et les infrastructures, tandis que les sociétés locales participent à peine à la définition des règles.
example_en: Digital colonialism takes root when foreign companies control data and infrastructure while local societies barely participate in defining the rules.
cloze: {{c1::Le colonialisme numérique}} s’enracine lorsque des entreprises étrangères contrôlent les données et les infrastructures, tandis que les sociétés locales participent à peine à la définition des règles.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from capitalization; the example fixes the structural domination sense rather than treating every foreign technology purchase as colonialism. Self-review restored the definite articles for natural French parallelism.

register: Ville intelligente is neutral in urban policy; the English loan remains frequent in consulting, municipal promotion and sectoral discourse.
trap: Smart does not translate as astucieuse here and the term is not limited to connectivity; it covers urban management through sensors, data and automation.
example_tl: La ville intelligente perd toute portée démocratique lorsqu’elle achète des capteurs avant de définir des objectifs publics et des limites contraignantes à l’usage des données.
example_en: The smart city loses all democratic substance when it buys sensors before defining public objectives and binding limits on data use.
cloze: {{c1::La ville intelligente}} perd toute portée démocratique lorsqu’elle achète des capteurs avant de définir des objectifs publics et des limites contraignantes à l’usage des données.
note: Old_back is accurate; the English loan is retained only as a marked sectoral alternative.

register: Critical term in intellectual history and technology commentary; the analytical alternative is transparent and slightly more formal.
trap: It is not optimism about one innovation: it attributes to technology the power to lead society toward an ideal order by itself.
example_tl: Le techno-utopisme des années quatre-vingt-dix a sous-estimé la rapidité avec laquelle la publicité, la surveillance et les plateformes fermées transformeraient les réseaux ouverts.
example_en: The techno-utopianism of the 1990s underestimated how quickly advertising, surveillance, and closed platforms would transform open networks.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-utopisme}} des années quatre-vingt-dix a sous-estimé la rapidité avec laquelle la publicité, la surveillance et les plateformes fermées transformeraient les réseaux ouverts.
note: Old_back identifies the correct lexeme but omits the article and unnecessarily capitalizes the common noun. Self-review restored articles in the coordinated subject for idiomatic prose.

register: Specialist social-science term; datafication is established in research, while mise en données is a transparent French analytical alternative.
trap: Datafication is not synonymous with numérisation: it specifically turns activities, relationships or qualities into quantifiable, processable data.
example_tl: La datafication de l’école modifie non seulement son administration, mais aussi les critères selon lesquels sont évalués les résultats, les comportements et les besoins d’accompagnement.
example_en: The datafication of schools changes not only their administration but also the criteria by which results, behavior, and support needs are assessed.
cloze: {{c1::La datafication}} de l’école modifie non seulement son administration, mais aussi les critères selon lesquels sont évalués les résultats, les comportements et les besoins d’accompagnement.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back supplies the accepted loan but incorrectly capitalizes the common noun. Self-review restored the articles before the coordinated evaluation targets.

tl: le paradoxe de la vie privée
register: Established behavioral-research and data-protection term for the apparent gap between stated privacy concern and observable disclosure behavior.
trap: The gap between stated concern and observed behavior does not prove indifference: platform design and a lack of alternatives constrain meaningful choice.
example_tl: Le paradoxe de la vie privée ne prouve pas que les usagers soient incohérents, puisque les interfaces manipulatrices et l’absence d’alternatives limitent leur capacité réelle de choisir.
example_en: The privacy paradox does not prove that users are inconsistent, since manipulative interfaces and the absence of alternatives limit their real ability to choose.
cloze: {{c1::Le paradoxe de la vie privée}} ne prouve pas que les usagers soient incohérents, puisque les interfaces manipulatrices et l’absence d’alternatives limitent leur capacité réelle de choisir.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review framed the example cautiously so the research label is not mistaken for a causal explanation, improved the final collocation, and removed a narrower confidentiality alternative.

register: Common journalistic and lifestyle label in France French; the full alternative is transparent but more clinical and less idiomatic in everyday media usage.
trap: It must not be confused with the droit à la déconnexion, the employment-law protection concerning work communications outside working hours.
example_tl: La détox numérique promet un soulagement individuel, mais ne modifie pas les modèles économiques qui transforment chaque minute passée hors ligne en manque à gagner.
example_en: Digital detox promises individual relief but does not change the business models that turn every minute spent offline into lost revenue.
cloze: {{c1::La détox numérique}} promet un soulagement individuel, mais ne modifie pas les modèles économiques qui transforment chaque minute passée hors ligne en manque à gagner.
note: Materially reorders old_back: désintoxication numérique is understandable, but détox numérique is the more idiomatic France-French production label. Self-review replaced a translated attention perdue metaphor with the natural manque à gagner.

register: Established media-economics and technology-criticism term for markets that capture, measure and monetize a scarce cognitive resource.
trap: It does not describe personal time management or an attentive economy; it names a system in which human attention becomes a commodity.
example_tl: L’économie de l’attention récompense davantage l’indignation immédiate que l’analyse rigoureuse, car les plateformes mesurent et monétisent plus facilement les réactions rapides.
example_en: The attention economy rewards immediate outrage more than rigorous analysis because platforms can measure and monetize rapid reactions more easily.
cloze: {{c1::L’économie de l’attention}} récompense davantage l’indignation immédiate que l’analyse rigoureuse, car les plateformes mesurent et monétisent plus facilement les réactions rapides.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; the contextual sentence fixes the specialist political-economic sense. Self-review replaced vendent with the more precise monétisent.

register: Standard public-policy and inequality-studies term; depending on context, it covers access, affordability, skills, service quality and outcomes.
trap: It is not limited to having an internet connection; equipment, usable speeds, skills and the ability to obtain essential services also matter.
example_tl: La fracture numérique persiste lorsque les foyers sont théoriquement raccordés, mais disposent d’équipements obsolètes, de débits insuffisants ou de services publics inaccessibles.
example_en: The digital divide persists when households are theoretically connected but have obsolete equipment, inadequate speeds, or inaccessible public services.
cloze: {{c1::La fracture numérique}} persiste lorsque les foyers sont théoriquement raccordés, mais disposent d’équipements obsolètes, de débits insuffisants ou de services publics inaccessibles.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate; the example prevents a narrow coverage-only reading.

register: Emerging critical term in geopolitics and technology policy; the paraphrastic alternative is more transparent in general prose.
trap: It is broader than surveillance alone: it concerns the use of digital infrastructures, automated decisions and information control to consolidate authoritarian power.
example_tl: Le techno-autoritarisme associe surveillance massive, censure automatisée et contrôle des infrastructures afin de rendre la contestation politique plus visible et plus coûteuse.
example_en: Techno-authoritarianism combines mass surveillance, automated censorship, and infrastructure control to make political dissent more visible and more costly.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-autoritarisme}} associe surveillance massive, censure automatisée et contrôle des infrastructures afin de rendre la contestation politique plus visible et plus coûteuse.
note: Old_back identifies the intended neologism but omits the article and capitalizes it unnecessarily.

register: Established privacy and digital-citizenship term for the accumulated records, inferred attributes and traces associated with a person’s digital activity.
trap: Empreinte numérique can also denote technology’s environmental footprint; in privacy contexts it includes passively collected and inferred data, not only deliberate posts.
example_tl: L’empreinte numérique d’une personne comprend des recherches, des déplacements et des métadonnées que des entreprises conservent même lorsqu’elle n’a jamais publié ces informations.
example_en: A person’s digital footprint includes searches, movements, and metadata that companies retain even when that person has never published that information.
cloze: {{c1::L’empreinte numérique}} d’une personne comprend des recherches, des déplacements et des métadonnées que des entreprises conservent même lorsqu’elle n’a jamais publié ces informations.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate; the trap records the genuine environmental ambiguity. Self-review restored the articles and removed a number-sensitive alternative.

register: Integrated institutional and policy term; masculine singular big data remains dominant in many technical and business settings in France.
trap: Do not calque the English adjective as grandes données; mégadonnées is plural, whereas the loan le big data normally takes singular agreement.
example_tl: Les mégadonnées permettent de repérer des tendances à grande échelle, mais leur volume ne corrige ni les échantillons biaisés ni les catégories construites selon des critères discriminatoires.
example_en: Big data makes it possible to identify large-scale trends, but its volume corrects neither biased samples nor categories built using discriminatory criteria.
cloze: {{c1::Les mégadonnées}} permettent de repérer des tendances à grande échelle, mais leur volume ne corrige ni les échantillons biaisés ni les catégories construites selon des critères discriminatoires.
note: Materially improves the unchanged English old_back by supplying the integrated French term and its required plural agreement. Self-review clarified that the category design, rather than the categories themselves, rests on discriminatory criteria.

register: Cloud computing is the dominant neutral technical term in France French; informatique en nuage is an institutional or explanatory alternative.
trap: Le cloud may name the remote environment or service offering, while cloud computing names the computing model; infonuagique is associated mainly with Canadian French.
example_tl: Le cloud computing réduit les coûts initiaux, mais enferme parfois les administrations dans des contrats opaques et les soumet à des juridictions étrangères.
example_en: Cloud computing reduces upfront costs but sometimes locks government agencies into opaque contracts and subjects them to foreign jurisdictions.
cloze: {{c1::Le cloud computing}} réduit les coûts initiaux, mais enferme parfois les administrations dans des contrats opaques et les soumet à des juridictions étrangères.
note: Materially reorders old_back: informatique en nuage is valid but marked, while the English loan is the usual production term in France. Self-review made administrations the contractual party and replaced an abstract dependency phrase with the precise jurisdictional risk.

register: Established interdisciplinary digital-policy concept; the singular construction is compact and classificatory, while the plural is natural in discursive prose.
trap: It is broader than réglementation des plateformes: it also includes private rules, design, moderation, appeals and participation by multiple actors.
example_tl: La gouvernance des plateformes ne se réduit pas au retrait de contenus, puisqu’elle détermine aussi qui fixe les règles et comment contester une décision.
example_en: Platform governance is not limited to content removal, since it also determines who sets the rules and how a decision can be challenged.
cloze: {{c1::La gouvernance des plateformes}} ne se réduit pas au retrait de contenus, puisqu’elle détermine aussi qui fixe les règles et comment contester une décision.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from its missing article and capitalization; the example supplies the concept’s broader institutional scope.

register: Marked Anglophone journalistic neologism, masculine in French; it benefits from explanation on first mention outside technology-policy circles.
trap: Techlash combines tech and backlash: it denotes a broad public and political reaction against Big Tech power, not a technical failure or one bad news cycle.
example_tl: Le techlash a placé des abus naguère traités comme des incidents isolés au centre du débat sur la concurrence, les données et le pouvoir économique.
example_en: The techlash placed abuses once treated as isolated incidents at the center of debate over competition, data, and economic power.
cloze: {{c1::Le techlash}} a placé des abus naguère traités comme des incidents isolés au centre du débat sur la concurrence, les données et le pouvoir économique.
note: Old_back identifies the loan but unnecessarily capitalizes it; the example fixes its collective backlash sense.

register: Established analytical and media term; the prefixed form is concise, while the transparent alternative fits less specialized prose.
trap: Techno-optimism does not necessarily entail techno-utopianism: confidence in innovation need not claim that technology alone will resolve social conflict.
example_tl: Le techno-optimisme gouvernemental présente l’intelligence artificielle comme un progrès inévitable et relègue ses coûts sociaux et environnementaux au rang d’effets secondaires.
example_en: The government’s techno-optimism presents artificial intelligence as inevitable progress and relegates its social and environmental costs to mere side effects.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-optimisme}} gouvernemental présente l’intelligence artificielle comme un progrès inévitable et relègue ses coûts sociaux et environnementaux au rang d’effets secondaires.
note: Old_back identifies the correct lexeme but omits the article and unnecessarily capitalizes the common noun.

register: Central but contested technology-policy concept; souveraineté technologique is related but can encompass broader industrial capabilities.
trap: It does not necessarily mean national autarky: it can concern public, collective or individual capacity to decide about data, standards and infrastructure.
example_tl: La souveraineté numérique européenne suppose de pouvoir auditer les systèmes critiques et changer de fournisseur, plutôt que d’interdire toute technologie étrangère.
example_en: European digital sovereignty requires the ability to audit critical systems and change providers rather than banning all foreign technology.
cloze: {{c1::La souveraineté numérique}} européenne suppose de pouvoir auditer les systèmes critiques et changer de fournisseur, plutôt que d’interdire toute technologie étrangère.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from the missing article and unnecessary capitalization; the trap distinguishes strategic capacity from isolation.

alts: la technologie au service de l’intérêt général
register: Emerging professional and academic field without a fully stabilized France-French label; the alternative is explanatory rather than terminological.
trap: Intérêt général does not simply mean popular or state-funded: it orients design, deployment and accountability toward collective needs and rights.
example_tl: La technologie d’intérêt général associe ingénieurs, juristes et citoyens afin que les services numériques protègent effectivement les droits et répondent aux besoins collectifs.
example_en: Public interest technology brings together engineers, lawyers, and citizens so that digital services effectively protect rights and address collective needs.
cloze: {{c1::La technologie d’intérêt général}} associe ingénieurs, juristes et citoyens afin que les services numériques protègent effectivement les droits et répondent aux besoins collectifs.
note: Materially diverges from old_back: intérêt public is understandable, but intérêt général is the idiomatic French public-policy collocation. Terminology remains unsettled, so the explicit paraphrase is retained as an alternative.

register: Culture numérique is natural in France-French education and policy prose; littératie numérique is a more explicit specialist research term.
trap: The concept is not limited to operating devices: it includes evaluating sources, understanding risks, creating content and participating critically and safely.
example_tl: La culture numérique permet de repérer les interfaces manipulatrices et de vérifier les sources, deux compétences aussi nécessaires que la maîtrise de nouvelles applications.
example_en: Digital literacy makes it possible to identify manipulative interfaces and verify sources, two skills as necessary as mastering new applications.
cloze: {{c1::La culture numérique}} permet de repérer les interfaces manipulatrices et de vérifier les sources, deux compétences aussi nécessaires que la maîtrise de nouvelles applications.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the mainstream France-French headword while recording the more exact but specialist littératie label, and clarified the apposition in the example.

register: Standard masculine technical borrowing in France French; as an adjective, open source is postpositive and invariable.
trap: Open source is not identical to logiciel libre: the movements overlap in licensing practice but frame their principles and goals differently.
example_tl: L’open source facilite l’audit indépendant des modèles, mais la publication du code ne garantit ni une communauté active ni une gouvernance transparente.
example_en: Open source facilitates independent auditing of models, but publishing the code guarantees neither an active community nor transparent governance.
cloze: {{c1::L’open source}} facilite l’audit indépendant des modèles, mais la publication du code ne garantit ni une communauté active ni une gouvernance transparente.
note: Old_back leaves the English expression articleless and capitalized; the production headword supplies French nominal syntax and lowercase styling.

register: Neutral technical and political term; web keeps the reference to web services rather than expanding the claim to all internet infrastructure.
trap: Décentralisé does not necessarily mean distribué: infrastructure may be spread across machines while decisive control or governance remains concentrated.
example_tl: Le web décentralisé cherche à réduire la dépendance à l’égard d’un intermédiaire unique, mais ses protocoles peuvent concentrer le pouvoir entre les mains de quelques développeurs.
example_en: The decentralized web seeks to reduce dependence on a single intermediary, but its protocols can concentrate power in the hands of a few developers.
cloze: {{c1::Le web décentralisé}} cherche à réduire la dépendance à l’égard d’un intermédiaire unique, mais ses protocoles peuvent concentrer le pouvoir entre les mains de quelques développeurs.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; the example avoids equating decentralized architecture with democratic governance. Self-review replaced two translated collocations with idiomatic French constructions.

register: Established umbrella term in media research and European policy; the adjectival alternative is compact and also current.
trap: It is broader than deliberate désinformation: it can also include misinformation and genuine material shared out of context to cause harm.
example_tl: Le désordre de l’information ne découle pas seulement d’informations fabriquées, mais aussi de faux contextes, de contenus manipulés et d’incitations algorithmiques opaques.
example_en: Information disorder arises not only from fabricated information but also from false contexts, manipulated content, and opaque algorithmic incentives.
cloze: {{c1::Le désordre de l’information}} ne découle pas seulement d’informations fabriquées, mais aussi de faux contextes, de contenus manipulés et d’incitations algorithmiques opaques.
note: Old_back identifies the concept but lacks the article and unnecessarily capitalizes it; the preferred form follows established European institutional usage. Self-review removed the ambiguous phrase nouvelles inventées.

register: Critical labor-sociology and political-economy term for workers whose subordinated labor sustains platforms, data supply chains and automated services.
trap: It does not denote everyone who uses digital devices: prolétariat retains a collective class sense grounded in economic subordination.
example_tl: Le prolétariat numérique assure la modération, l’annotation et la livraison dont dépendent les plateformes, tout en restant privé de pouvoir sur leurs infrastructures.
example_en: The digital proletariat handles the moderation, annotation, and delivery on which platforms depend while remaining deprived of power over their infrastructures.
cloze: {{c1::Le prolétariat numérique}} assure la modération, l’annotation et la livraison dont dépendent les plateformes, tout en restant privé de pouvoir sur leurs infrastructures.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization in the source context. Self-review made the class relation explicit so the label does not encompass every technology user.

register: Established critical term in political economy and data studies for the process of making data into tradable commodities.
trap: Marchandisation is broader than commercialisation or monétisation: data can acquire commodity form before any visible sale or revenue is realized.
example_tl: La marchandisation des données transforme des traces d’usage en actifs échangeables, bien avant que leur vente directe ou leur monétisation ne devienne visible.
example_en: The commodification of data turns usage traces into tradable assets, long before their direct sale or monetization becomes visible.
cloze: {{c1::La marchandisation des données}} transforme des traces d’usage en actifs échangeables, bien avant que leur vente directe ou leur monétisation ne devienne visible.
note: Old_back supplies the established French term but unnecessarily capitalizes its article. Self-review excluded narrower commercialisation and monétisation from the alternatives.

register: Contested digital-economy framework that treats certain data-generating contributions as labor potentially deserving recognition or remuneration.
trap: Le travail des données usually means work performed on data, while les données comme main-d’œuvre wrongly turns labor into a workforce.
example_tl: Les données comme travail constituent un cadre qui propose de rémunérer certaines contributions informationnelles, mais ses détracteurs contestent l’assimilation de toute trace à un travail.
example_en: Data as labor is a framework that proposes remunerating certain informational contributions, but its critics dispute treating every trace as work.
cloze: {{c1::Les données comme travail}} constituent un cadre qui propose de rémunérer certaines contributions informationnelles, mais ses détracteurs contestent l’assimilation de toute trace à un travail.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review marks the proposal as contested and distinguishes the fixed frame from work carried out on data.

register: Marxian expression extended in technology criticism to platforms, models, data centers, software and other productive digital infrastructure.
trap: Moyens de production names productive assets; mode de production also includes property, labor relations and the wider social organization of production.
example_tl: Les moyens de production numériques incluent les centres de données, les logiciels et les modèles, mais leur propriété détermine aussi qui organise le travail et capte la valeur.
example_en: The digital means of production include data centers, software, and models, but their ownership also determines who organizes labor and captures value.
cloze: {{c1::Les moyens de production numériques}} incluent les centres de données, les logiciels et les modèles, mais leur propriété détermine aussi qui organise le travail et capte la valeur.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained this beside mode de production numérique because the two occupy distinct Marxian analytical levels.

register: Critical labor-studies term for extraction and discipline organized or intensified through algorithmic management; the alternative is more analytically explicit.
trap: Algorithmique does not make an algorithm an intentional exploiter; responsibility remains with the institutions that design and deploy the system.
example_tl: L’exploitation algorithmique intensifie les cadences des livreurs par des objectifs opaques, sans soustraire les plateformes à leur responsabilité dans l’organisation du travail.
example_en: Algorithmic exploitation intensifies couriers’ pace through opaque targets without absolving platforms of responsibility for organizing the work.
cloze: {{c1::L’exploitation algorithmique}} intensifie les cadences des livreurs par des objectifs opaques, sans soustraire les plateformes à leur responsabilité dans l’organisation du travail.
note: Old_back gives the conventional compact label. Self-review added the more cautious alternative to clarify algorithmic mediation without erasing institutional agency.

register: Established social-economy and platform-studies term for a movement based on collective ownership and democratic governance of digital platforms.
trap: Coopérativisme de plateforme names the model or movement; une plateforme coopérative is one concrete organization and is not interchangeable in every sentence.
example_tl: Le coopérativisme de plateforme permet aux chauffeurs de détenir collectivement l’application, d’élire sa direction et de répartir les revenus selon des règles débattues.
example_en: Platform cooperativism allows drivers to own the app collectively, elect its management, and distribute revenue according to collectively debated rules.
cloze: {{c1::Le coopérativisme de plateforme}} permet aux chauffeurs de détenir collectivement l’application, d’élire sa direction et de répartir les revenus selon des règles débattues.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review kept the singular de plateforme found in French specialist usage and excluded the name of an individual cooperative.

register: Established and normally critical concept in sociology, media studies and the history of technology.
trap: It is stronger than saying that a technology has effects: it assigns technology an autonomous or predominant causal role in social change.
example_tl: Le déterminisme technologique attribue aux réseaux sociaux une force politique autonome, alors que leurs effets dépendent aussi des institutions, des usages et des intérêts économiques.
example_en: Technological determinism attributes autonomous political force to social networks, although their effects also depend on institutions, uses, and economic interests.
cloze: {{c1::Le déterminisme technologique}} attribue aux réseaux sociaux une force politique autonome, alors que leurs effets dépendent aussi des institutions, des usages et des intérêts économiques.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review made the concept’s strong causal claim explicit rather than presenting it as any account of technological effects.

register: Established but still specialized data-policy and geopolitical term for subordinating data use and flows to national interests.
trap: It is not synonymous with souveraineté des données, which can emphasize decision-making capacity or rights without the same nationalist priority.
example_tl: Le nationalisme des données pousse certains États à imposer un stockage local et à restreindre les flux, afin que l’exploitation des données serve prioritairement les intérêts nationaux.
example_en: Data nationalism pushes some states to require local storage and restrict flows so that the exploitation of data primarily serves national interests.
cloze: {{c1::Le nationalisme des données}} pousse certains États à imposer un stockage local et à restreindre les flux, afin que l’exploitation des données serve prioritairement les intérêts nationaux.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review retained the institutional French term, distinguished it from data sovereignty, and replaced the vague localiser les flux with concrete policy actions.

register: Established commons and digital-policy vocabulary; the alternative is more explanatory, while communs foregrounds a resource, community and governance arrangement.
trap: A commun is not merely free of charge or in the public domain: it also entails a community and rules for collective stewardship.
example_tl: Les communs numériques reposent sur une ressource partagée, une communauté active et des règles de gouvernance, non sur la seule gratuité de l’accès.
example_en: Digital commons rest on a shared resource, an active community, and governance rules, not merely on free access.
cloze: {{c1::Les communs numériques}} reposent sur une ressource partagée, une communauté active et des règles de gouvernance, non sur la seule gratuité de l’accès.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back is valid as the explanatory alternative; self-review promoted the compact specialist term used in French commons research.

register: Strongly critical geopolitical and political-economy label alleging structural domination through technology firms, infrastructure, standards and dependencies.
trap: This is a stronger accusation than international reach or technological dependence: impérialisme asserts hierarchy, extraction and projection of power.
example_tl: L’impérialisme technologique mondial se manifeste lorsque quelques entreprises imposent leurs infrastructures et leurs normes, tout en maintenant les marchés périphériques dans une relation de dépendance.
example_en: Global tech imperialism appears when a few companies impose their infrastructure and standards while keeping peripheral markets in a relationship of dependency.
cloze: {{c1::L’impérialisme technologique mondial}} se manifeste lorsque quelques entreprises imposent leurs infrastructures et leurs normes, tout en maintenant les marchés périphériques dans une relation de dépendance.
note: Old_back is defensible after lowercasing its article. Self-review retained the item because its marked domination claim cannot be replaced by a neutral phrase about global technology firms.

register: Specialist Marxian extension encompassing productive forces, ownership, labor relations and forms of accumulation organized through digital systems.
trap: Mode de production is broader than moyens de production: it includes the social relations organizing the tools and infrastructure, not just those assets.
example_tl: Le mode de production numérique ne désigne pas seulement des outils connectés, mais aussi les rapports de propriété, de travail et d’accumulation qui organisent l’économie.
example_en: The digital mode of production denotes not only connected tools but also the relations of ownership, labor, and accumulation that organize the economy.
cloze: {{c1::Le mode de production numérique}} ne désigne pas seulement des outils connectés, mais aussi les rapports de propriété, de travail et d’accumulation qui organisent l’économie.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review retained this beside moyens de production numériques and removed a pronoun whose antecedent blurred the distinction between tools and social relations.

register: Specialist critical term in science and technology studies for science and technology treated as a coupled, market-oriented system.
trap: Technoscience is normally written as one word in French and denotes the entanglement of science and technology, not a simple list of both activities.
example_tl: La technoscience néolibérale subordonne les priorités de recherche aux brevets, aux marchés et aux indicateurs de rentabilité, au détriment de besoins collectivement définis.
example_en: Neoliberal technoscience subordinates research priorities to patents, markets, and profitability indicators at the expense of collectively defined needs.
cloze: {{c1::La technoscience néolibérale}} subordonne les priorités de recherche aux brevets, aux marchés et aux indicateurs de rentabilité, au détriment de besoins collectivement définis.
note: Materially normalizes old_back’s hyphenated techno-science to the established closed form. Self-review fixed the coupled STS sense in both the register line and example.

register: Rare intellectual-history and critical-theory label for Marxist analysis of computer networks, cyberculture and digital capitalism.
trap: The label does not mean left-wing online activism in general; cyber- refers here to networks and cybernetics rather than specifically to cybersecurity.
example_tl: Le cybermarxisme relit l’exploitation et la lutte des classes à partir des réseaux informatiques, sans supposer que la technologie abolisse les rapports capitalistes.
example_en: Cyber-Marxism rereads exploitation and class struggle through computer networks without assuming that technology abolishes capitalist relations.
cloze: {{c1::Le cybermarxisme}} relit l’exploitation et la lutte des classes à partir des réseaux informatiques, sans supposer que la technologie abolisse les rapports capitalistes.
note: Materially normalizes old_back’s hyphenated form to the regular closed French prefix form. Confidence is moderate because the label is rare; the register line makes that restriction explicit.

register: Specialist social-theory concept associated especially with Manuel Castells and his account of the network society.
trap: Informationnalisme has two consecutive n’s and is not synonymous with société de l’information or informatisation; it names a distinct developmental logic.
example_tl: L’informationnalisme désigne chez Castells un mode de développement où la production de valeur dépend surtout de la génération, du traitement et de la circulation de l’information.
example_en: For Castells, informationalism denotes a mode of development in which value production depends primarily on generating, processing, and circulating information.
cloze: {{c1::L’informationnalisme}} désigne chez Castells un mode de développement où la production de valeur dépend surtout de la génération, du traitement et de la circulation de l’information.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s misspelling informationalisme to the established French informationnalisme. Self-review anchored this low-frequency term to its principal theoretical tradition.

register: Established social-theory term, especially associated with Castells, for capitalism structured by information processing and networks.
trap: It is not merely a stylistic synonym for capitalisme numérique: informationnel points to a specific theory of productivity, networks and power.
example_tl: Le capitalisme informationnel organise la productivité et le pouvoir autour de réseaux capables de traiter l’information, plutôt qu’autour de la seule numérisation des échanges.
example_en: Informational capitalism organizes productivity and power around networks able to process information, rather than around the mere digitization of exchanges.
cloze: {{c1::Le capitalisme informationnel}} organise la productivité et le pouvoir autour de réseaux capables de traiter l’information, plutôt qu’autour de la seule numérisation des échanges.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review preserved the Castells-associated adjective instead of flattening the term into generic digital capitalism.

register: Critical commons and political-economy metaphor extending the historical enclosure of shared land to knowledge, code, data and digital infrastructure.
trap: Enfermement means confinement; enclosure is retained in French scholarship because it evokes the privatization and restriction of access to shared resources.
example_tl: L’enclosure numérique convertit un commun accessible en espace propriétaire, en fermant les interfaces ou en imposant des droits exclusifs sur les ressources partagées.
example_en: Digital enclosure turns an accessible commons into a proprietary space by closing interfaces or imposing exclusive rights over shared resources.
cloze: {{c1::L’enclosure numérique}} convertit un commun accessible en espace propriétaire, en fermant les interfaces ou en imposant des droits exclusifs sur les ressources partagées.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s enfermement numérique, which loses the historical commons metaphor. Self-review used the attested French borrowing and fixed its privatization sense contextually.

register: Frequent geopolitical and journalistic metaphor for systemic technology rivalry, especially over infrastructure, standards, research and supply chains.
trap: The metaphor normally covers more than a trade dispute: it can imply rival technology blocs, security controls and competing industrial systems.
example_tl: La guerre froide technologique se joue désormais à coups de contrôles sur les semi-conducteurs, de subventions industrielles et de batailles normatives.
example_en: The tech cold war is now being waged through semiconductor controls, industrial subsidies, and battles over standards.
cloze: {{c1::La guerre froide technologique}} se joue désormais à coups de contrôles sur les semi-conducteurs, de subventions industrielles et de batailles normatives.
note: Old_back is lexically sound after lowercasing the common-noun metaphor. Self-review replaced a generic rivalry example with concrete mechanisms spanning trade, industry and standards.

tl: les Routes de la soie numériques
register: Established geopolitical and infrastructure-policy name for the digital component of China’s Belt and Road Initiative; French institutional usage often favors the plural.
trap: The literal Ceinture et Route numériques is not the conventional French name; French policy writing uses Route or Routes de la soie numériques.
example_tl: Les Routes de la soie numériques associent câbles, centres de données et promotion de normes chinoises, tout en renforçant l’influence de Pékin.
example_en: The Digital Silk Roads combine cables, data centers, and the promotion of Chinese standards while strengthening Beijing’s influence.
cloze: {{c1::Les Routes de la soie numériques}} associent câbles, centres de données et promotion de normes chinoises, tout en renforçant l’influence de Pékin.
note: Materially replaces old_back’s literal Ceinture et Route numériques with the established French name. Self-review removed a number-changing alternative that was not directly substitutable in the example and repaired an overextended use of déployer.

register: Established innovation-policy and geopolitical term for linking national power, security and autonomy to domestic technological capacity.
trap: It is broader than nationalisme des données because it also covers industrial capacity, research, standards, procurement and supply chains.
example_tl: Le techno-nationalisme lie la maîtrise des semi-conducteurs à la sécurité nationale et justifie des subventions, des contrôles d’exportation ainsi qu’une préférence pour les fournisseurs nationaux.
example_en: Techno-nationalism links mastery of semiconductors to national security and justifies subsidies, export controls, and a preference for domestic suppliers.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-nationalisme}} lie la maîtrise des semi-conducteurs à la sécurité nationale et justifie des subventions, des contrôles d’exportation ainsi qu’une préférence pour les fournisseurs nationaux.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Independent review found both hyphenated and closed French spellings, so the latter is retained as a genuine orthographic alternative.

tl: le fétichisme de la marchandise numérique
register: Highly theoretical Marxian expression extending commodity fetishism to digital goods and services.
trap: Fétichisme has its Marxian sense here: social and material relations appear as properties of the commodity, not as an individual’s personal obsession.
example_tl: Le fétichisme de la marchandise numérique masque le travail, les minerais et l’énergie incorporés dans un service présenté comme immatériel et spontanément disponible.
example_en: Digital commodity fetishism conceals the labor, minerals, and energy embodied in a service presented as immaterial and spontaneously available.
cloze: {{c1::Le fétichisme de la marchandise numérique}} masque le travail, les minerais et l’énergie incorporés dans un service présenté comme immatériel et spontanément disponible.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review used material infrastructure in the example to secure the specialized Marxian sense.

register: Specialist Marxian digital-labor term whose exact source and measurement vary across authors and models of user contribution.
trap: In Marxian French, surplus value is plus-value, not valeur ajoutée, which ordinarily denotes an accounting or tax concept.
example_tl: La plus-value numérique proviendrait, selon cette approche, de l’écart entre la valeur créée par les activités en ligne et la rémunération versée aux contributeurs.
example_en: According to this approach, digital surplus value would arise from the gap between value created by online activities and compensation paid to contributors.
cloze: {{c1::La plus-value numérique}} proviendrait, selon cette approche, de l’écart entre la valeur créée par les activités en ligne et la rémunération versée aux contributeurs.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review added a conditional and attribution because accounts of user-produced digital surplus value remain theoretically contested.

register: Emerging critical political-economy concept; the main form is idiomatic analytical French, while the direct calque is rarer and more theory-bound.
trap: Rente is not limited to property rental: it can arise from controlling scarce access, intellectual property, interfaces or markets rather than creating new goods.
example_tl: Le capitalisme rentier numérique tire ses revenus du contrôle d’interfaces, de brevets et d’effets de réseau, davantage que de la création de nouveaux biens.
example_en: Digital rentier capitalism derives its revenue from controlling interfaces, patents, and network effects more than from creating new goods.
cloze: {{c1::Le capitalisme rentier numérique}} tire ses revenus du contrôle d’interfaces, de brevets et d’effets de réseau, davantage que de la création de nouveaux biens.
note: Materially improves old_back by promoting the more idiomatic capitalisme rentier numérique; the direct rentiérisme calque remains intelligible but is less established. Self-review preserved that register difference.

register: Formal international-relations term for institutions, standards and multistakeholder processes governing technologies with cross-border reach.
trap: Gouvernance is broader than gouvernement or réglementation: it includes coordination, standards, firms and civil society as well as binding state rules.
example_tl: La gouvernance mondiale des technologies associe États, entreprises et société civile pour fixer des normes transfrontalières que la seule réglementation nationale ne peut imposer.
example_en: Global technology governance brings together states, companies, and civil society to set cross-border standards that national regulation alone cannot impose.
cloze: {{c1::La gouvernance mondiale des technologies}} associe États, entreprises et société civile pour fixer des normes transfrontalières que la seule réglementation nationale ne peut imposer.
note: Materially improves old_back: des technologies clearly marks the object governed, whereas gouvernance technologique can suggest governance carried out by technological means.

register: Historical and theoretical term for socialist projects using information, feedback and computation to coordinate economic planning.
trap: Cybernétique refers here to the classical science of feedback, communication and control, not to the narrower modern sense of internet security.
example_tl: Le socialisme cybernétique mobilise information, rétroaction et calcul pour coordonner la production, comme l’illustra le projet Cybersyn au Chili dans les années 1970.
example_en: Cybernetic socialism uses information, feedback, and computation to coordinate production, as the Cybersyn project in 1970s Chile illustrated.
cloze: {{c1::Le socialisme cybernétique}} mobilise information, rétroaction et calcul pour coordonner la production, comme l’illustra le projet Cybersyn au Chili dans les années 1970.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. Self-review anchored the concept historically and avoided conflating classical cybernetics with contemporary cybersecurity.

register: Critical labor and surveillance expression; dispositifs is idiomatic analytical French when concrete systems and procedures are at issue.
trap: Contrôle may also mean neutral checking or supervision; here it means the capacity to direct, discipline or sanction behavior through algorithmic systems.
example_tl: Les dispositifs algorithmiques de contrôle attribuent les tâches, évaluent les performances et déclenchent des sanctions, tout en dissimulant les choix patronaux derrière des scores.
example_en: Algorithmic means of control assign tasks, assess performance, and trigger sanctions while concealing managerial choices behind scores.
cloze: {{c1::Les dispositifs algorithmiques de contrôle}} attribuent les tâches, évaluent les performances et déclenchent des sanctions, tout en dissimulant les choix patronaux derrière des scores.
note: Materially improves old_back by preferring dispositifs in this procedural sense; the literal phrase remains a valid alternative. Self-review kept institutional choices visible in the example.

alts: la base et la superstructure numériques
register: Highly theoretical Marxian frame adapting the relation between the economic base and legal, political or cultural superstructure to digital society.
trap: French Marxian usage conventionally pairs infrastructure with superstructure; base does not mean a database here, and numériques agrees with both coordinated nouns.
example_tl: L’infrastructure et la superstructure numériques s’influencent réciproquement lorsque la propriété des plateformes façonne le droit, tandis que les institutions redéfinissent les marchés.
example_en: The digital base and superstructure influence each other when platform ownership shapes law while institutions redefine markets.
cloze: {{c1::L’infrastructure et la superstructure numériques}} s’influencent réciproquement lorsque la propriété des plateformes façonne le droit, tandis que les institutions redéfinissent les marchés.
note: Materially improves old_back by promoting the conventional French Marxian pair infrastructure et superstructure. Self-review retained the literal variant and avoided claiming a mechanically one-way relation.

register: Specialist public-policy and sociology term for governing conduct through automated scoring, ranking or rule enforcement; the alternative makes the instrument explicit.
trap: Régulation algorithmique means regulation performed through algorithms; regulation of algorithms is la régulation des algorithmes, with des rather than par.
example_tl: La régulation algorithmique module l’accès aux prestations selon des scores opaques, transformant des choix administratifs contestables en décisions apparemment techniques.
example_en: Algorithmic regulation adjusts access to benefits according to opaque scores, turning contestable administrative choices into apparently technical decisions.
cloze: {{c1::La régulation algorithmique}} module l’accès aux prestations selon des scores opaques, transformant des choix administratifs contestables en décisions apparemment techniques.
note: Old_back is formally accurate but leaves the direction of regulation ambiguous. Self-review fixed the through-algorithms sense in both the register line and example.

register: Specialist critical term in internet law and policy for claims that online activity is fundamentally unlike older domains and should escape ordinary legal analogies or rules.
trap: Exceptionnalisme does not mean excellence or an Internet exception already written into law; it names a doctrine asserting the medium’s fundamental singularity.
example_tl: L’exceptionnalisme d’Internet conduit certains dirigeants à présenter les plateformes comme un domaine inédit, auquel les règles ordinaires de responsabilité ne s’appliqueraient pas.
example_en: Internet exceptionalism leads some executives to present platforms as an unprecedented domain to which ordinary rules of liability supposedly do not apply.
cloze: {{c1::L’exceptionnalisme d’Internet}} conduit certains dirigeants à présenter les plateformes comme un domaine inédit, auquel les règles ordinaires de responsabilité ne s’appliqueraient pas.
note: Old_back gives the right concept but the compact d’Internet construction is more idiomatic here. Self-review added the conditional to mark the claim as contested rather than factual.

register: Emerging, strongly critical geopolitical label for domination exercised through concentrated cloud infrastructure, contractual dependence and extraterritorial legal reach.
trap: The phrase makes a structural domination claim; it is not a neutral synonym for foreign cloud provision or a large provider’s international presence.
example_tl: L’impérialisme du cloud s’installe lorsque des administrations dépendent d’infrastructures étrangères dont elles ne maîtrisent ni les conditions contractuelles, ni les clés, ni les voies de recours.
example_en: Cloud imperialism takes hold when public administrations depend on foreign infrastructure whose contractual terms, keys, and avenues for redress they do not control.
cloze: {{c1::L’impérialisme du cloud}} s’installe lorsque des administrations dépendent d’infrastructures étrangères dont elles ne maîtrisent ni les conditions contractuelles, ni les clés, ni les voies de recours.
note: Old_back is defensible after lowercasing the article. Confidence is moderate because the label remains emerging; self-review stated its evaluative register explicitly and replaced an unnatural claim about mastering a jurisdiction.

register: Economy and labor-policy term for income organized as successive short assignments; the alternative is common and more journalistic or socially evaluative.
trap: The legacy économie gigogne is nonsensical: gig means a short paid job here, whereas gigogne describes objects nested inside one another.
example_tl: L’économie à la tâche promet de la flexibilité aux livreurs, mais fait peser sur eux les temps d’attente non rémunérés, l’entretien du véhicule et le risque économique.
example_en: The gig economy promises couriers flexibility but makes them bear unpaid waiting time, vehicle maintenance, and economic risk.
cloze: {{c1::L’économie à la tâche}} promet de la flexibilité aux livreurs, mais fait peser sur eux les temps d’attente non rémunérés, l’entretien du véhicule et le risque économique.
note: Materially replaces old_back’s false translation économie gigogne. The exact-duplicate report assigns this source item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB; self-review excluded the broader économie des plateformes and repaired the verb governing the shifted burdens.

register: Established competition-policy and advertising metaphor for company-controlled platform environments; the alternative is explanatory and less figurative.
trap: A jardin clos is not merely a secure private network: the criticism concerns an operator controlling access, interoperability, data and commercial relations within an ecosystem.
example_tl: Les jardins clos des plateformes retiennent les utilisateurs et les annonceurs en limitant l’interopérabilité, l’accès aux données et la mesure indépendante des campagnes.
example_en: Corporate platform walled gardens retain users and advertisers by limiting interoperability, access to data, and independent measurement of campaigns.
cloze: {{c1::Les jardins clos des plateformes}} retiennent les utilisateurs et les annonceurs en limitant l’interopérabilité, l’accès aux données et la mesure indépendante des campagnes.
note: Old_back translates the metaphor but entreprises is too indiscriminate for the platform-market sense. Self-review chose the established platform complement and retained a nonfigurative alternative.

register: Critical political and intellectual-history label for combining faith in technology and markets with radical distrust of state regulation; both spellings circulate.
trap: Libertarien is not libertaire: French libertaire usually evokes anarchist traditions, while libertarianisme foregrounds individual property rights and minimal government.
example_tl: Le technolibertarianisme érige l’innovation privée en principe politique et dépeint souvent l’impôt, la régulation et les services publics comme des entraves illégitimes.
example_en: Techno-libertarianism elevates private innovation into a political principle and often portrays taxation, regulation, and public services as illegitimate constraints.
cloze: {{c1::Le technolibertarianisme}} érige l’innovation privée en principe politique et dépeint souvent l’impôt, la régulation et les services publics comme des entraves illégitimes.
note: Materially normalizes old_back’s less common techno-libertarisme and preserves an attested hyphenated spelling. Self-review made the distinction from libertaire explicit.

register: Neutral in computing for retrieving data, but critical in political economy when it frames systematic appropriation of behavioral traces as an extractive process.
trap: The headword alone does not choose between technical retrieval and critical appropriation; extractivisme des données is a related, stronger systemic diagnosis, not a free synonym.
example_tl: L’extraction de données transforme chaque clic en ressource exploitable, alors même que les utilisateurs ignorent souvent quelles inférences commerciales seront tirées de leurs traces.
example_en: Data extraction turns every click into an exploitable resource even though users often do not know what commercial inferences will be drawn from their traces.
cloze: {{c1::L’extraction de données}} transforme chaque clic en ressource exploitable, alors même que les utilisateurs ignorent souvent quelles inférences commerciales seront tirées de leurs traces.
note: Old_back is lexically accurate but underspecifies the source sense. Self-review anchored the critical big-tech reading without promoting the stronger data-extractivism label to an alternative.

register: Strongly critical political-economy metaphor comparing platform ownership and rent extraction to private lordship; techno-féodalisme is prominent in current French debate.
trap: The metaphor does not claim a literal return to medieval institutions; it alleges durable private control of infrastructure, dependence and rent capture.
example_tl: Le techno-féodalisme décrit des plateformes propriétaires qui prélèvent une rente sur les échanges, tout en fixant unilatéralement les règles d’accès à leur domaine.
example_en: Digital feudalism describes proprietary platforms that levy rent on exchanges while unilaterally setting the rules for access to their domain.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-féodalisme}} décrit des plateformes propriétaires qui prélèvent une rente sur les échanges, tout en fixant unilatéralement les règles d’accès à leur domaine.
note: Materially promotes the prominent French label techno-féodalisme over old_back’s defensible literal form, retained as an alternative. Self-review marked the expression as a contested metaphor.

register: Media-theory and democratic-theory term extending the public-sphere concept to digitally mediated debate, visibility and opinion formation.
trap: The term does not mean every publicly accessible website; sphère publique denotes a social arena in which issues become visible and collective opinion is formed.
example_tl: La sphère publique numérique élargit l’accès au débat, mais les choix de classement des plateformes déterminent en grande partie quelles voix y deviennent visibles.
example_en: The digital public sphere broadens access to debate, but platforms’ ranking choices largely determine which voices become visible there.
cloze: {{c1::La sphère publique numérique}} élargit l’accès au débat, mais les choix de classement des plateformes déterminent en grande partie quelles voix y deviennent visibles.
note: Old_back is accurate after lowercasing the article. Self-review made the public-sphere meaning explicit and replaced an abstract visibility collocation with more idiomatic French.

register: Established copyright and media-technology term, usually retaining the English initialism DRM in French professional usage.
trap: Despite gestion des droits, DRM denotes technical controls on access, copying or use; it is not the administration of users’ digital rights.
example_tl: La gestion des droits numériques (DRM) peut limiter la copie d’un livre acheté légalement et rendre sa consultation dépendante d’un service distant.
example_en: Digital rights management (DRM) can restrict copying of a legally purchased book and make access to it dependent on a remote service.
cloze: {{c1::La gestion des droits numériques (DRM)}} peut limiter la copie d’un livre acheté légalement et rendre sa consultation dépendante d’un service distant.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from the missing article. Self-review preserved DRM because it is the conventional French professional initialism and clarified the term’s potentially misleading wording.

alts: la dépendance à l’égard des plateformes
register: Neutral-to-critical platform-economy term for structural reliance on an intermediary’s audience, infrastructure, rules or interfaces; the alternative is more formal.
trap: This is not personal compulsive use of a platform; the policy sense concerns an organization’s reduced ability to operate, bargain or exit independently.
example_tl: La dépendance aux plateformes fragilise les éditeurs lorsque leurs revenus, leur audience et l’accès à leurs abonnés reposent sur des règles modifiables sans négociation.
example_en: Platform dependency weakens publishers when their revenue, audience, and access to subscribers rely on rules that can be changed without negotiation.
cloze: {{c1::La dépendance aux plateformes}} fragilise les éditeurs lorsque leurs revenus, leur audience et l’accès à leurs abonnés reposent sur des règles modifiables sans négociation.
note: Old_back is accurate but heavier than the idiomatic aux construction. Self-review distinguished structural dependence from individual overuse and verified that the formal alternative remains substitutable.

register: Established economics and competition-policy term for changes in a service’s value as the number or composition of its users changes.
trap: Effets de réseau are not simply impacts on a communications network; the causal mechanism runs through participation on the same or another side of a market.
example_tl: Les effets de réseau renforcent une messagerie dominante : plus elle rassemble d’utilisateurs, plus chaque membre a intérêt à y rester pour joindre ses contacts.
example_en: Network effects strengthen a dominant messaging service: the more users it brings together, the more reason each member has to stay and reach their contacts.
cloze: {{c1::Les effets de réseau}} renforcent une messagerie dominante : plus elle rassemble d’utilisateurs, plus chaque membre a intérêt à y rester pour joindre ses contacts.
note: Old_back is accurate after lowercasing the article. Self-review replaced an awkward contacts construction with a natural same-side participation mechanism distinct from generic scale economies.

register: Specialist STS and political-communication term for the political ordering embedded in technical systems or, in some literature, strategic political action through technology.
trap: The term does not merely mean public policy about technology; it foregrounds how technical design itself organizes power or enables political action.
example_tl: La technopolitique apparaît dans l’architecture d’une identité numérique lorsque ses choix techniques déterminent qui peut être reconnu, surveillé ou exclu d’un service.
example_en: Technopolitics appears in the architecture of a digital identity system when its technical choices determine who can be recognized, monitored, or excluded from a service.
cloze: {{c1::La technopolitique}} apparaît dans l’architecture d’une identité numérique lorsque ses choix techniques déterminent qui peut être reconnu, surveillé ou exclu d’un service.
note: Old_back is accurate after lowercasing and closing the compound. Confidence is moderate because two specialist traditions use the term; self-review fixes the STS sense in the example.

register: Established but marked geopolitical metaphor for the division of a globally interoperable internet into nationally, technically or commercially bounded segments; the alternative is neutral.
trap: Balkanisation is evaluative and implies damaging fragmentation; it should not be used as a neutral synonym for decentralization or harmless regional variation.
example_tl: La balkanisation d’Internet progresse lorsque des États imposent des passerelles nationales, des normes incompatibles et des blocages qui empêchent les services de circuler librement.
example_en: Internet balkanization advances when states impose national gateways, incompatible standards, and blocking measures that prevent services from circulating freely.
cloze: {{c1::La balkanisation d’Internet}} progresse lorsque des États imposent des passerelles nationales, des normes incompatibles et des blocages qui empêchent les services de circuler librement.
note: Old_back is accurate after lowercasing the article. Self-review retained neutral fragmentation as an alternative while marking the source metaphor’s negative judgment.

register: Critical geopolitical term for leadership sustained across infrastructure, standards, markets and ideas, not merely by possession of advanced devices.
trap: Hégémonie is stronger than market leadership but not identical to impérialisme: it can operate through standards, consent and imitation as well as coercive dependence.
example_tl: L’hégémonie technologique mondiale se consolide lorsqu’un petit nombre d’acteurs impose ses normes, ses infrastructures et sa vision du progrès comme références universelles.
example_en: Global tech hegemony becomes entrenched when a small number of actors impose their standards, infrastructure, and vision of progress as universal reference points.
cloze: {{c1::L’hégémonie technologique mondiale}} se consolide lorsqu’un petit nombre d’acteurs impose ses normes, ses infrastructures et sa vision du progrès comme références universelles.
note: Old_back is accurate after supplying an article and regular capitalization. Self-review retained this beside cloud imperialism because hegemony includes consensual normative leadership, not only extractive domination.

register: Established data-policy term for requirements or choices concerning the country or territory where data is stored, and sometimes processed.
trap: It is unrelated to geolocation data about people or devices; the term concerns the place of storage or processing, and does not by itself guarantee sovereign control.
example_tl: La localisation des données peut imposer un stockage national, sans empêcher qu’un fournisseur étranger y conserve un accès ou reste soumis au droit de son pays.
example_en: Data localization can require domestic storage without preventing a foreign provider from retaining access or remaining subject to its home country’s laws.
cloze: {{c1::La localisation des données}} peut imposer un stockage national, sans empêcher qu’un fournisseur étranger y conserve un accès ou reste soumis au droit de son pays.
note: Old_back is accurate after adding the article. Self-review separated physical location from legal control and corrected the illogical suggestion that a jurisdiction itself accesses data.

register: Standard technical and institutional France-French term for making information unreadable without the appropriate key.
trap: The legacy cryptage is widely used but technically discouraged; do not confuse chiffrement with hachage, which is designed as a one-way transformation.
example_tl: Le chiffrement de bout en bout protège le contenu pendant son transit, à condition que les appareils et les clés des correspondants restent sûrs.
example_en: End-to-end encryption protects content while it is in transit, provided that the correspondents’ devices and keys remain secure.
cloze: {{c1::Le chiffrement}} de bout en bout protège le contenu pendant son transit, à condition que les appareils et les clés des correspondants restent sûrs.
note: Materially corrects old_back’s cryptage to the term preferred by French technical authorities. Self-review avoided claiming that encryption protects compromised endpoints.

register: Established legal and policy rendering in France and the EU when data privacy concerns the rights and safeguards governing personal-data processing.
trap: Confidentialité des données is too narrow: confidentiality prevents unauthorized disclosure, while data privacy also concerns lawful purposes, minimization, access and individual rights.
example_tl: La protection des données personnelles exige davantage que le secret des fichiers : elle encadre aussi leur collecte, leur finalité, leur durée de conservation et leur rectification.
example_en: Data privacy requires more than keeping files secret: it also governs their collection, purpose, retention period, and correction.
cloze: {{c1::La protection des données personnelles}} exige davantage que le secret des fichiers : elle encadre aussi leur collecte, leur finalité, leur durée de conservation et leur rectification.
note: Materially replaces old_back’s overly narrow confidentialité des données with the established EU legal frame. Self-review made the broader scope concrete without treating privacy and data protection as universally identical.

register: Established international-policy term covering the institutions and processes through which states, firms, technical bodies and civil society shape internet rules and resources.
trap: Gouvernance is broader than gouvernement or réglementation: internet naming, protocols and standards are coordinated by multiple public, private and technical actors.
example_tl: La gouvernance de l’Internet associe les États, les entreprises, les organismes techniques et la société civile, même si leur influence réelle demeure profondément inégale selon les enceintes.
example_en: Internet governance brings together states, companies, technical bodies, and civil society, even though their actual influence remains deeply unequal across forums.
cloze: {{c1::La gouvernance de l’Internet}} associe les États, les entreprises, les organismes techniques et la société civile, même si leur influence réelle demeure profondément inégale selon les enceintes.
note: Old_back is accurate after adding the article. Self-review foregrounded the multistakeholder scope, avoided the idealized claim that all participants wield equal power, and restored natural articles in the enumeration.

register: Established public-policy and security term whose scope ranges from attributes and credentials used for authentication to a person’s broader online representation.
trap: Identité numérique is not automatically a digital ID card, nor is it synonymous with empreinte numérique, which denotes traces left by activity.
example_tl: L’identité numérique publique doit permettre de prouver un droit précis sans obliger l’usager à révéler davantage d’informations que le service n’en exige.
example_en: A public digital identity system should make it possible to prove a specific entitlement without requiring users to reveal more information than the service needs.
cloze: {{c1::L’identité numérique}} publique doit permettre de prouver un droit précis sans obliger l’usager à révéler davantage d’informations que le service n’en exige.
note: Old_back is accurate after adding the article. Self-review used an authentication example and explicitly distinguished the broader term from both a credential and a digital footprint.

register: Geopolitical and internet-control term for a state-scale filtering architecture; it is often used critically or descriptively by analogy with China’s Great Firewall.
trap: This is not simply a government agency’s network firewall: national describes the scale of filtering and control imposed on traffic crossing a country’s networks.
example_tl: Le pare-feu national bloque des médias étrangers et ralentit les outils de contournement, tout en donnant aux autorités un levier sur l’accès à l’information.
